item.title: Sean McVay: Flight was great, guys seem fresh, we'll be ready to rock
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Rams' flight to Melbourne landed on Thursday morning local time, which left them with about 28 hours to acclimate to Australia before their game against the 49ers gets underway.
item.content:encoded:
The Rams' flight to Melbourne landed on Thursday morning local time, which left them with about 28 hours to acclimate to Australia before their game against the 49ers gets underway.

The choice to arrive so close to the game — the 49ers have been in Melbourne for days — has been scrutinized all week, but head coach Sean McVay said at a press conference after arriving that he thinks his team will be ready to go when it is time to kick things off.

"Flight was great," McVay said, via Olivia Garvey of NBC Los Angeles. "We’re well rested, we feel good. It really was. Matthew [Stafford] and I were just talking about that on the way over here. Able to sleep through the night, guys were comfortable, they seem fresh. Get a good night rest tonight and be ready to rock tomorrow."

In addition to giving one team an early boost in the NFC West race, the difference in the approaches to the game will make the result a referendum on how teams should plan for trips to play in any future Australian games.

item.title: Will Anderson on facing the Bills: An AFC Championship matchup
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: A perusal of the many published predictions for the 2026 season finds a lot of support for the Bills and Texans as two of the strongest teams in the AFC.
item.content:encoded:
A perusal of the many published predictions for the 2026 season finds a lot of support for the Bills and Texans as two of the strongest teams in the AFC.

One of them is likely to exit Week 1 with an 0-1 record, however. The two teams will meet in Houston on Sunday afternoon in a matchup that Texans defensive end Will Anderson believes will be a preview of one of the games that both teams hope to be playing in come January.

“This is an AFC Championship matchup," Anderson said in a Wednesday press conference. "Two really good teams. We have a ton of respect for them. Josh Allen leading the way, really great offensive line. James Cook, best running back in the league. . . . The type of atmosphere that I’m feeling like it’s gonna be on Sunday is gonna be that AFC Championship-type feel."

The Texans pass rush got the best of Allen and the Bills last November. Anderson had 2.5 sacks in that game and the Texans will be looking for something similar as they try to get an early leg up in the race for the actual AFC Championship Game.

item.title: Mike Vrabel: You can't throw three interceptions, Drake Maye knows that
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel pointed to quarterback Drake Maye's turnovers as the difference after losing to the Seahawks.
item.content:encoded:
Patriots coach Mike Vrabel pointed to quarterback Drake Maye's turnovers as the difference after losing to the Seahawks.

"You can't throw three interceptions. Drake knows that," Vrabel said.

The Patriots lost the game 13-10 and lost the turnover battle 3-0, as all three turnovers in the game were Maye interceptions. Given that, it's no surprise that the Patriots lost: Last season, teams that were minus-3 or worse in turnover margin went 3-38.

"We can't turn the ball over and we have to create more turnovers," Vrabel said. "There's a few things we have to eliminate that get you beat in this league."

The Patriots' loss was sealed when Maye threw an interception into the end zone with 21 seconds left. Vrabel defended the decision to try to score a game-winning touchdown rather than settle for a game-tying field goal, but he acknowledged the throw wasn't what the Patriots wanted.

"We're trying to be aggressive and win the football game, but not reckless," Vrabel said. "It's never just about one guy. I think everybody knows that."

It's not about one guy, but the Patriots' loss to the Seahawks was primarily attributable to one guy: Maye wasn't good enough.

item.title: Drake Maye: My bad decisions cost us the game
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: "That wasn't how I play football and how I want to represent my game and playing quarterback for the Patriots," Maye said after losing to the Seahawks.
item.content:encoded:
Patriots quarterback Drake Maye took the blame after throwing three interceptions in a 13-10 loss to the Seahawks to open the NFL season on Wednesday night.

"I thought we had the game under control," Maye said. "I lost patience and it cost us. There were decisions that cost us the game, on my part, on my end. I vow to myself to be better and realize it's a long season, but at the same time you can't have those. It was unacceptable and I know I have to get back to work, because that wasn't how I play football and how I want to represent my game and playing quarterback for the Patriots."

With the Patriots trailing by a field goal and in field goal range in the final minute, Maye knew a turnover was the one thing the Patriots couldn't afford. And yet he threw a pass into the end zone that Seattle's Josh Jobe intercepted, sealing the Patriots' loss.

"It was just unacceptable. We had a chance to send it to overtime, at the worst, and the only thing you could do was turn the ball over, and that's what I did."

Maye had a tremendous 2025 season, finishing second in MVP voting and leading the Patriots to the Super Bowl. But they lost the Super Bowl to the Seahawks, and los to the Seahawks again in Week 1, and Maye knows he needs to be better.

item.title: Ernest Jones: When you think about Seattle, we want you to think about defense
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Seahawks didn't put any points on the board until the fourth quarter on Wednesday night, but waiting to get the scoring started didn't keep them from coming up with a win.
item.content:encoded:
The Seahawks didn't put any points on the board until the fourth quarter on Wednesday night, but waiting to get the scoring started didn't keep them from coming up with a win.

Their defense forced four punts while spotting the Patriots a 10-0 lead and then came up with interceptions on New England's final three possessions to help pave the way to a 13-10 comeback win that played out with quarterback Sam Darnold out of the game to be evaluated for a hip injury. The Seahawks also sacked Drake Maye three times in the second half and generally sent notice to the NFL that the unit that propelled them to the Super Bowl last season remain in fine shape.

"When you think about Seattle, we want you to think about our defense, and what we are going to bring each and every day," linebacker Ernest Jones said, via the team's website.

The Seahawks pulled off Wednesday's performance without safeties Nick Emmanwori and Ty Okada, so they'll have even more weapons at their disposal in the weeks to come and that's not great news for the opposing offenses on their schedule.

item.title: Panthers restructure DL Tershawn Wharton's contract
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Panthers have created some more cap room ahead of Week 1.
item.content:encoded:
The Panthers have created some more cap room ahead of Week 1.

Per Spotrac, they have restructured defensive lineman Tershawn Wharton's contract. They converted $12.2 million of his base salary into a signing bonus, which opened up $9.7 million in cap space for the coming season.

Wharton is in the second season of a three-year deal and the team added three void years to further spread out the remaining cap hit in coming seasons.

While Wharton is helping the team's salary cap situation, he won't be helping them against the Bears on Sunday. Wharton had neck surgery this offseason and is on the physically unable to perform list to open the regular season.

item.title: Harrison Smith: I kind of knew I'd be back the whole time
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Vikings fans saluted Harrison Smith's entire career when he walked off the field at the end of Week 18 last season, but thoughts that it was the final time the safety would be on the field were premature.
item.content:encoded:
Vikings fans saluted Harrison Smith's entire career when he walked off the field at the end of Week 18 last season, but thoughts that it was the final time the safety would be on the field were premature.

Smith was out of contract throughout the offseason and preseason, but remained in touch with head coach Kevin O'Connell and agreed to return for a 15th season a few days ago. While that came as a pleasant surprise to many in Minnesota, it was something that Smith had in mind for quite a while.

"I think I kind of knew it the whole time. I just didn't know, exactly, the timing," Smith said, via the team's website.

Neither Smith nor O'Connell is ready to say that the safety will play against the Packers in Week 1. Smith has worked out with a return in mind, but acknowledged the big difference between that training and what he'll be called to do on the field.

"I'm in good shape. I've been working out," Smith said. "But there's nothing like playing football. It's just the reality of it. Heart rate, outside factors, thinking a lot while you're moving. It's hard to simulate that. I kind of do it the best I can. There's something about being on the grass and thinking while you're moving. You can feel a little stuck sometimes and just getting the fluidity back. That's kind of what I've been able to do the last few years — be very fluid out there while I'm thinking."

Smith wasn't on the injury report for Wednesday, but further word on his status for Sunday will likely come closer to kickoff.

item.content:encoded:
The 49ers are set to welcome two of their biggest stars back to the lineup for their first game of the 2026 season.

Neither tight end George Kittle nor defensive end Nick Bosa received injury designations on the team's final injury report ahead of their game against the Rams in Melbourne, Australia. Kittle is returning from a torn Achilles while Bosa has been working his way back from a torn ACL.

Head coach Kyle Shanahan said this week that the team would be "smart" with both players given the extent of their injuries, so they may not play a full complement of snaps on Thursday.

Defensive lineman James Thompson is listed as questionable while defensive lineman Alfred Collins has been ruled out after suffering a torn patellar tendon in practice earlier this week.

item.title: Drew Lock on TD pass to Jaxon Smith-Njigba: Definitely never practiced that play
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: One of the realities of life as an NFL backup quarterback is that you get fewer opportunities in practice and that means there are some plays that you never get to rehearse ahead of time.
item.content:encoded:
One of the realities of life as an NFL backup quarterback is that you get fewer opportunities in practice and that means there are some plays that you never get to rehearse ahead of time.

That's the situation Seahawks quarterback Drew Lock found himself in after replacing the injured Sam Darnold during Wednesday night's game against the Patriots. With the Seahawks down 10-3 and facing a fourth-and-1 from the New England 45-yard line with under 12 minutes to play, offensive coordinator Brian Fleury sent in a play that Lock had never gotten the chance to try out on the practice field.

It was a play-action pass to wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba that picked up the first down and then much more once Smith-Njigba turned around to find room to run all the way to the end zone.

"It is like a classic football play," Lock said, via the team's website. "But, no. No, definitely never ran it. Looked kind of funny before the snap. I didn't really seem like they had anybody ready to match Jaxon based on what I knew we were about it run. He's the third read in that play, and when 11 is just standing there, you got to give him the pill."

The Seahawks struggled to move the ball most of the night, but Drake Maye kept giving the ball away for the Patriots and Lock came up with key completions to Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp to set up Seattle's go-ahead field goal. He finished the night 16-of-22 for 187 yards and said after the game that he trusted in the defense to keep the game within reach.

"Knowing the type of defense that we have, there is no rush to push the ball down the field," Lock said. "Let's find ways to get the ball in our guys' hands. Now, when the ones down field are there, I've never been one to be afraid of those, but having the mindset of taking football, getting it in our guys' hands. You got the best defense in the world, in my opinion, let's keep the ball moving forward and see what the scoreboard looks like at the end of this."

The Seahawks can be happy with how the scoreboard looks thanks in large part to how well Lock handled being thrown into the fire on the second series of the 2026 season.

item.title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba had 122 of the Seahawks' 200 receiving yards, and Seattle's only TD
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: "It's not all on me," Smith-Njigba said. "It's a team effort."
item.content:encoded:
On an NFL opening night when the Seahawks' offense was otherwise stalling, wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba kept it going.

Smith-Njigba caught a short pass on fourth-and-1 and raced downfield for a 45-yard touchdown reception in the fourth quarter, scoring the Seahawks' only touchdown in the 13-10 win over the Patriots. Afterward, he credited the play call, quarterback Drew Lock and his teammates' blocking more than his own effort.

"I was happy it was a pass play," Smith-Njigba said. "My job was to find a zone and Drew did a great job finding me, and afterward just do what I do, try to get upfield and protect the ball. Great upfield blocking by our tight ends."

The Seahawks' passing game went 8-for-11 for 122 yards and a touchdown when throwing to Smith-Njigba and 9-for-13 for 78 yards and no touchdowns when throwing to everyone else on the team. Despite that, Smith-Njigba credited teammates Cooper Kupp and Rashid Shaheed, who had a combined three catches for 39 yards.

"It's not all on me. We have Cooper Kupp making big plays, we have Sheed making big plays," Smith-Njigba said. "It's a team effort."

It is a team effort, but Smith-Njigba showed who the best player on the team is.

item.title: PFT's Week 1 2026 NFL picks
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: My not-for-betting purposes look at all 16 opening-weekend games.
item.content:encoded:
The 2026 season returns tonight, and we'll be doing things a little bit differently when it comes to the weekly effort to predict what may happen in the upcoming slate of games.

For decades, I've had my own thoughts about who will, or won't, win in a given weekend. Thanks to the fact that my dad was a bookie, and given his incessant messaging that it's impossible for the bettor to win over the long haul, I've had no inclination to wager on games.

When the floodgates for legalized, normalized, and monetized sports betting opened eight years ago, my relationship with the burgeoning industry became complicated, to say the least. There's plenty of money to be made in sports media by aligning with one, or more, of the various sportsbooks and, more recently, prediction markets. I've declined to pursue any direct deals, due in large part to the reality that the ease of app-based betting has spawned, and will continue to create, generations of folks who fail to understand that, over time, it's a losing proposition. (And, of course, the small minority who figure out a way to win consistently will inevitably be cut off.)

I've used this platform to be candid about the realities of betting, in the hopes of dissuading young men with still-developing brains from thinking it's a path to getting rich quick or, even worse, from believing it's a replacement for the more traditional means for making ends meet. I've previously balanced those concerns with taping weekly podcasts in which Simms and I made picks for every game against the spread.

It bugged me. It gnawed at me. Starting this year, I decided to stop doing it.

But what about my views on the coming games? Is it possible to pick winners and losers for the sheer fun of it, with no skin in the game — and without sending the message, directly or indirectly, that others should rely on my views when making their wagering decisions?

I decided to lay out my weekly picks, for amusement purposes only. "Amusement purposes only" used to be code for "go ahead and bet." Now, it's truly for amusement purposes only. With the addition of a clear caveat that you should only wager what you can afford to lose. Over time, you will.

Have a budget. Stick to it. And never, ever chase your losses. The gambling money should come from your entertainment budget. Use only the money you'd otherwise spend for movies, video games, steaming services, books (I've got four you can chose from, with more coming), and do not go beyond that. When the budgeted amount is gone, it's gone.

I'll reiterate that message every week, mainly because too few of the people in sports media who are grabbing the bag from sportsbooks and prediction markets will ever bother to tell the members of their audience the truth about gambling. As my dad the bookie started telling me more than 50 years ago, you can't win.

With that, here's my own personal look at each of the games. Do not rely on anything I say if you choose to devote any of your entertainment budget to betting on the games.

Patriots at Seahawks (Wednesday)

For the third time, a Super Bowl rematch happens in Week 1. The Patriots have beefed up the passing game, with A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs. Quarterback Drake Maye and left tackle Will Campbell are healthy. The Seahawks lost Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III to free agency. Rookie Jadarian Price carries the load, with Zach Charbonnet (knee) starting the season on the PUP list. And Seattle has a brand-new, first-time offensive coordinator in Brian Fleury, thanks to Klint Kubiak doing the job well enough in one year to become a head coach.

It won't be easy for the Patriots, who were blown out by the Seahawks at a neutral site in February. But they have receivers Brown and Doubs. Maye is healthy. And they seem to be rallying around coach Mike Vrabel, after his eventful offseason. It's a pure hunch. And I'd rather be wrong by being bold than to take the chalk and regret missing the potential signs for an opening-night upset.

Patriots 24, Seahawks 21.

49ers vs. Rams in Australia (Thursday)

The Rams reacted to a close-but-no-cigar 2025 season by adding defensive end Myles Garrett. Which sparked defensive tackle Aaron Donald's unretirement. And while Donald didn't make the trip to Melbourne, the Rams have enough to overcome a 49ers team that has had one bizarre thing after another happen to it this year.

While health will be a key factor as to whether the Rams can get to the Super Bowl and win it, they're healthy for now. And they seem to fully believe in their plan to barnstorm in and out of Australia.

Rams 24, 49ers 13.

Bills at Texans

Few teams have ever faced more pressure than the Bills carry into 2026. The coach was fired after losing in overtime in the divisional round. The G.M. was promoted, as was the offensive coordinator. And the campaign starts with a trip to face the best defense in the NFL, which may be even better in 2026.

Yes, the offense is a major question mark for the Texans. They should be able to do enough to hold serve in a home game that could serve as the first step toward winning the top seed in the AFC.

Texans 20, Bills 16.

Buccaneers at Bengals

The Bucs relish the opportunity to get things started on the road, and quarterback Baker Mayfield's new contract removes one significant potential distraction. But the Bengals know the stakes. A fourth straight season without a playoff berth will result in major changes.

For now, Cincinnati quarterback Joe Burrow sees parallels to his 2019 LSU team, which won a national championship. That's enough to get me to give them the edge at home in what could be one of the most exciting games of the first weekend of the season.

Bengals 27, Buccaneers 24.

Bears at Panthers

Carolina won a none-of-the-above division last year, thanks to the Falcons beating the Saints on the final Sunday. The Bears traded to Carolina the pick that became quarterback Bryce Young, and that allowed the Bears (since Carolina bottomed out in 2023) to land MVP contender Caleb Wiliams.

It will be a challenging year for the Bears as the hunted in the NFC North. For now, their Week 1 Panther hunt should be successful.

Bears 24, Panthers 17.

Saints at Lions

Lions coach Dan Campbell believes the team's Super Bowl window is still open. They have the talent to justify his faith. Now, they just have to prove it. A strong Week 1 start against a sneaky-good Saints team will help set the tone.

Much of it hinges on new offensive coordinator Drew Petzing. With running back Jahmyr Gibbs now the centerpiece of the offense, it becomes much easier for any offensive coach to look like Bill Walsh.

Lions 34, Saints 24.

Ravens at Colts.

The team that fled Baltimore in 1984 hosts the team that backfilled the vacancy 12 years later. It's a tough opener for a new coaching staff, but the Ravens have Lamar Jackson — and he seems to be a big believer in the new offense.

Ravens 24, Colts 20.

Falcons at Steelers

The post-Mike Tomlin era begins with what should be an easy win against Tua Tagovailoa, who won the QB1 job by default. The Steelers are 14-2-1 vs. the Falcons since the AFL-NFL merger. A loss would spark widespread panic in Pittsburgh, especially against a quarterback with a reputation for panicking when the first read is covered.

Steelers 21, Falcons 10.

Jets at Titans

Robert Saleh is saying all the right things publicly. Privately, he surely relishes the chance to stick it to the owner who prematurely pulled the plug on what could have been a potential playoff contender in 2024. The question is whether the Titans have enough talent to outscore the Jets. Home team gets the edge.

Titans 20, Jets 17.

Browns at Jaguars

Deshaun Watson gets a two-game audition in Florida, with the goal of doing enough to get the folks in Cleveland to accept him for Week 3 and Week 4. The Jaguars feel disrespected and overlooked; Sunday gives them a chance to put the world on notice that they'll be a force in 2026.

Jaguars 28, Browns 14.

Commanders at Eagles

Before training camp, the Commanders landed in the group of teams that could break either way in 2026. It feels like it's about to break badly for Washington. And it doesn't help that they have to visit one of the best teams in the league to start the season.

Eagles 27, Commanders 14.

Packers at Vikings

The Packers have neither running back Josh Jacobs nor linebacker Micah Parsons. The Vikings are quietly optimistic about a team with a great defense and an offense that can't be much worse than it was in 2025. Will they commit to their new outside zone running game? Will Kyler Murray turn back the clock to 2021? Week 1 will show plenty about whether the Vikings can continue their trend of making the playoffs every other year.

Vikings 30, Packers 20.

Cardinals at Chargers

Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh has a 6-0 record in regular-season openers. He gets a winnable game and the first opportunity to get more out of an offense, with Mike McDaniel in charge, that has been good enough to win in the regular season but not good enough to advance in the playoffs. The Cardinals are a work in progress at best, stuck behind a trio of Super Bowl contenders in their own division.

Chargers 27, Cardinals 10.

Dolphins at Raiders

A pair of first-time coaches get together in Las Vegas, with new quarterbacks and generally overmatched rosters. Between them, they have a 48-year streak without playoff wins. Both are long shots to end those runs in 2026, because both are long shots to qualify for the postseason. But, hey, someone has to win this game. Unless there's a tie.

And while both teams seem to constantly change, one thing has been fairly constant. Since 2000, the Dolphins are 12-3 against the Raiders. Between that, De'Von Achane, and a focus on putting a new culture in place, Miami gets a win in one of their rare winnable 2026 games.

Dolphins 13, Raiders 10.

Cowboys at Giants (Sunday night)

The Giants hired John Harbaugh with the goal of sparking a dramatic turnaround. What better way to do that than to overcome one of their biggest rivals on the weekend of the 25th anniversary of 9/11?

Giants 23, Cowboys 21.

Broncos at Chiefs (Monday night)

Patrick Mahomes is back. While he may not be better than ever, given his knee injury, the Chiefs will settle for as good as before. It won't be easy and they may need a few jump balls from the football gods, but it just feels like a great way for the Chiefs to turn the page on a surprisingly poor 2025 showing.

Chiefs 20, Broncos 17.

item.title: NFL Kickoff 2026: Seahawks beat Patriots 13-10, but lose Sam Darnold to hip injury
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Seattle's defense picked off Drake Maye three times, including late in the fourth quarter to clinch the Week 1 victory.
item.content:encoded:
The Seahawks beat the Patriots 13-10 after raising the banner for beating the same club in Super Bowl LX.

But Seattle’s celebration will likely be a bit muted, as the club has a significant injury concern with its quarterback.

Sam Darnold exited the contest after Seattle’s first series of the season with a hip injury and did not return. Darnold was sacked by Dre’Mont Jones on third-and-6 from the New England 46 — Seattle’s sixth play from scrimmage.

Darnold came off the field with a noticeable limp. He was examined in the sideline medical tent before going to the locker room for further evaluation, which was when he was announced as questionable.

Just before halftime, Seattle downgraded Darnold to out.

The quarterback completed one of his two passes for 13 yards, which was a completion to Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

Drew Lock replaced Darnold on the second drive and played the rest of the game.

On the other side, Patriots quarterback Drake Maye threw three interceptions, the last of which took New England out of the game.

With just 26 seconds left in regulation and the Patriots facing third-and-5 from Seattle’s 16-yard line, Maye was flushed out of the pocket to his right and inexplicably threw a poor jump ball to Mack Hollins in the end zone. But Josh Jobe caught the ball instead, effectively ending the contest.

The Patriots had taken a conservative offensive approach for most of the game and had a 10-3 lead entering the fourth quarter. But that’s when the meltdown started, as Maye attempted a deep pass to Romeo Doubs that was intercepted by Nathaniel Pritchett on the second play of the period.

That led to Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s 45-yard touchdown catch-and-run that tied the game at 10-10.

On New England’s next possession, Romeo Doubs had a critical drop on a second-and-14 play. Doubs was wide open after Maye was able to evade the pass rush in the backfield and roll to his right. But Doubs was unable to handle the throw as it fell incomplete.

On the next play, Maye fired a pass over the middle for DeMario Douglas, but Julian Love read the play perfectly and picked the ball off to give Seattle another opportunity.

Seattle took advantage of it with Jason Myers’ 26-yard field goal to go up by three.

That’s all the Seahawks needed, as Maye threw his final interception to lose the contest.

Maye finished 22-of-33 for 178 yards with one touchdown and three interceptions. Maye did not have a multi-interception game last year until Super Bowl LX, also against the Seahawks. He also had 47 rushing yards on seven attempts.

Lock was 16-of-22 for 187 yards with one touchdown in relief of Darnold.

Notably, Patriots receiver A.J. Brown also suffered an ankle injury early in the third quarter and did not return.

Now at 1-0, the Seahawks will have a long layoff before facing the division-rival Cardinals on the road in Week 2.

The 0-1 Patriots will be at home to face the Steelers on Sunday, Sept. 20.

item.title: Report: Deshaun Watson was cited for speeding on August 26
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The eventful month for Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson included a speeding ticket, two days after he was named the starter.
item.content:encoded:
The eventful month for Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson included a speeding ticket, two days after he was named the starter.

Via Fox 8 in Cleveland, Watson was cited for driving 86 miles per hour in a 60 mph zone on Wednesday, August 26.

Watson entered a plea of not guilty in Cleveland municipal court on Wednesday. A bench trial is set for Wednesday, September 23.

That's a work day for Watson. It makes sense to just accept the ticket and move on; surely, he won't be missing practice before the team's home opener.

The citation also happened four days after the low point of his Cleveland career — a preseason appearance that featured incessant booing, and a regrettable postgame press conference during which he expressed doubt as to whether he could play effectively during a future home game.

Whether he plays in the Week 3 home game surely depends largely on how he and the team perform in the first two games of the season, at Jacksonville and at Tampa Bay.

item.title: Mike Macdonald: Sam Darnold did not suffer hip fracture, more tests to come
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Seahawks received some positive news on quarterback Sam Darnold, but the extent of his hip injury is still unclear.
item.content:encoded:
The Seahawks received some positive news on quarterback Sam Darnold, but the extent of his hip injury is still unclear.

In his postgame press conference on Wednesday night, head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters that doctors were able to rule out a fracture.

"Let’s say it’s good news right now. I know our thoughts and prayers are with Sam — we love him. The guys really pulled through for him," Macdonald said. "At this point, we were able to rule out a fracture. So, there’s some more tests to be done. But that’s what I’m saying when it’s positive, but I know — we’re still working through all that, but right now a fracture is out, which is great news."

Darnold exited the game in the first quarter after he was sacked on third down to end Seattle's first possession. After limping off the field, he was examined in the sideline medical tent before limping back up to the locker room for further examination.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that Darnold was transported to Harborview Medical Center to undergo a CT scan on his hip. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport noted Darnold received positive news on the CT scan and his X-Ray, indicating that he was able to avoid a major injury. But Darnold is scheduled for an MRI on Thursday to confirm the diagnosis.

Given the lack of clarity on the injury, Macdonald said he didn't know what Darnold's status would be for Seattle's Week 2 matchup against Arizona.

Brown went down with an ankle injury early in the third quarter of Wednesday's 13-10 loss to the Seahawks to open the 2026 season and did not return.

"I don’t have any update yet," head coach Mike Vrabel said postgame. "Wasn't able to return, obviously."

Brown was injured on an incomplete pass from Drake Maye on third down. The ball was low, leading to Seahawks cornerback Nehemiah Pritchett landing awkwardly on Brown’s lower leg/ankle area as he broke up the pass.

Brown stayed down for a bit before trainers came to assist him. He limped off the field and was examined in the sideline medical tent before limping up to the locker room for further examination.

Brown’s Patriots debut ended with him catching three passes on four targets for 26 yards.

The reigning AP offensive player of the year just showed why he earned the honor.

But from there, the receiver did the rest, turning on the burners to evade defenders for a 45-yard score.

Smith-Njigba gained 41 yards after the catch.

item.title: NFL Kickoff 2026: Patriots lead Seahawks 7-0 at halftime
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Patriots lead the Seahawks 7-0 at halftime, but Seattle has a bigger concern moving forward.
item.content:encoded:
The Patriots lead the Seahawks 7-0 at halftime, but Seattle has a bigger concern moving forward.

Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold exited the game after the first series with a hip injury. He appeared to suffer it when he was sacked by Dre’Mont Jones on third down, which brought up a punt.

Darnold limped to the sideline before he was eventually examined in the medical tent. He then limped off the field up to the locker room for further evaluation.

Just before halftime, the Seahawks ruled him out.

Backup Drew Lock played the rest of the first half for Seattle. So far, he’s completed 6-of-8 passes for 51 yards. But the Seahawks have also struggled to move the ball, registering six first downs.

On the other side, Drake Maye has been a lot more effective than he was against Seattle’s defense in Super Bowl LX back in February. He’s gotten off some quick passes and used his legs effectively to scramble. Though Maye’s most productive pass was one that wasn’t even completed — as newcomer A.J. Brown drew a defensive pass interference penalty that put the Patriots at Seattle’s 2-yard line.

On the next play, Maye tossed a 2-yard touchdown to rookie tight end Eli Rairdon for the NFL’s first touchdown of 2026.

Maye finished the first half 10-of-12 for 66 yards with a touchdown.

The Patriots have 10 first downs, 130 yards, and are 3-of-7 on third down.

Seattle has 120 yards and is 1-of-6 on third down. They may want to have a heavy dose of rookie Jadarian Price in the second half, who has 42 yards on his six carries in his debut.

The Patriots will receive the second-half kickoff.

item.title: Joey Porter Jr. is "up in the air" for Sunday
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: With Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon and Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez getting their new contracts, another 2023 draft pick at the same position is still waiting for his reward.
item.content:encoded:
With Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon and Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez getting their new contracts, another 2023 draft pick at the same position is still waiting for his reward.

Per a source with knowledge of the negotiations, nothing is imminent. However, the two sides have been talking.

Porter, the first pick in round two (and the 32nd overall that year because the Dolphins had been stripped of their first-round pick), is due to make $3.924 million in 2026, the final year of his deal. If he doesn't get a new contract by Sunday, it's "up in the air," we're told, as to whether he'll play.

Complicating matters is the Steelers' policy against negotiating once the regular season begins. So if a contract isn't done by Sunday, ii won't be this year — unless the Steelers deviate from their outdated policy.

The two sides obviously disagree on the amount to be paid for a cornerback who has yet to make it to a Pro Bowl. And it's unclear whether the gap can be bridged.

Absent a deal, will Porter play? It will be hard for the team to question the legitimacy of a back problem (he was limited in practice on Wednesday), and he could sit indefinitely in protest of the prospect of playing for less than $4 million.

Another issue is the fact that Porter's father, Joey Porter Sr., who played in the NFL for 13 seasons and who is definitely involved in the situation. Joey Sr.'s knowledge of how the sausage gets made becomes a factor in whether a deal gets done, and whether Joey Jr. will take the best offer on the table before the season starts.

However it goes, it needs to go somewhere — or nowhere — quickly. And if they don't finalize a contract, it could get awkward and potentially ugly.

item.title: Rams land in Melbourne some 28 hours before kickoff
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Rams landed in Melbourne at 7 a.m. local time ahead of their season opener against the 49ers.
item.content:encoded:
The Rams landed in Melbourne at 7 a.m. local time ahead of their season opener against the 49ers.

They left Tuesday night PT and flew the nearly 8,000 miles in 16 hours.

The game kicks off at 8:35 p.m. ET on Thursday, which is 10:35 a.m. on Friday, Sept. 11, in Melbourne. Thus, the Rams landed roughly 28 hours before kickoff.

The NFL posted video of their arrival, with coach Sean McVay and wide receiver Puka Nacua among those walking down the jetway.

Unlike the 49ers, who landed in Melbourne almost a week ago, the Rams chose to stay on Pacific Time. They will go to sleep in the late afternoon Melbourne time, wake up in the middle of the night and play the game on Friday morning before heading straight back to Los Angeles afterward.

item.content:encoded:
Outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard returned to practice on Wednesday, and the Eagles' practice report shows he was limited.

That was expected as he works his way back from a pectoral injury.

Greenard missed all of training camp after straining a pectoral muscle while lifting weights earlier in the summer. He went on the active/physically unable to perform list but chose not to move him to reserve/PUP.

That indicates the Eagles expect Greenard to play sometime in the first four weeks.

The Eagles traded for Greenard in April, sending two third-round draft picks to the Vikings for the star pass rusher. Philadelphia then signed him to a four-year, $100 million extension.

Rookie tight end Eli Stowers (hamstring) was the only other player on the team's injury report. He also was limited.

He is among the Seahawks' inactives.

Safety Ty Okada (hamstring) also will not play, having been ruled out ahead of the game.

Emmanwori did not participate in any of the team’s open practices during camp as he works his way back from arthroscopic surgery in July to repair his right ankle. He initially injured the ankle during the 2025 season opener and then aggravated it in a Super Bowl LX practice.

Wide receiver Tory Horton (hamstring), quarterback Jalen Milroe, offensive guard Beau Stephens, tight end Nick Kallerup and defensive lineman Mike Morris are the Seahawks' other inactives. Milroe will serve as the emergency third quarterback.

The Patriots' inactives are center Ben Brown (knee), cornerback Karon Prunty, linebacker Erick Hunte, quarterback Behren Morton, running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle), offensive lineman Walter Rouse and wide receiver Efton Chism III. Morton will serve as the emergency third quarterback.

item.title: 49ers DT James Thompson returns to limited work, while Nick Bosa, George Kittle remain limited
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The 49ers had only one change to their injury report Wednesday: Defensive tackle James Thompson (hamstring) returned to limited work.
item.content:encoded:
The 49ers had only one change to their injury report Wednesday: Defensive tackle James Thompson (hamstring) returned to limited work. Thompson did not practice a day earlier.

That is good news for a team that lost defensive tackle Alfred Collins to a knee injury earlier this week.

Defensive end Nick Bosa (knee) and tight end George Kittle (Achilles) remained limited ahead of Thursday night's season opener.

Bosa tore the ACL in his right knee in a Sept. 21 game against the Cardinals and underwent surgery Sept. 26. As he was coming back this summer, Bosa experienced soreness and tendinitis, and the 49ers backed him down until Sept. 2 when he returned to practice.

49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris said recently Bosa will play, but it is unclear how much.

Kittle's status sounds more up in the air as he works his way back from the right Achilles he tore in a Jan. 11 playoff game against the Eagles. Like Bosa, if Kittle plays, he likely is on a snap count.

Linebacker Luke Gifford (hamstring), linebacker Dre Greenlaw (Achilles), defensive tackle Gracen Halton (ankle), defensive end Romello Height (ankle) and fullback Kyle Juszczyk (finger) again were limited.

Cornerback Upton Stout (Achilles) remained a full participant.

item.title: George Pickens: Greg Newsome should feel how he feels, but we disagree
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Cowboys wide receivers CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens combined for 168 catches, 2,506 yards and 12 touchdowns last season.
item.content:encoded:
Cowboys wide receivers CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens combined for 168 catches, 2,506 yards and 12 touchdowns last season. Only Detroit's duo of Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams had more yards, and only by 12.

While acknowledging the Cowboys' top wideouts as "great players," Giants cornerback Greg Newsome also said he is part of the "best cornerback room in the league" and likes his and his teammates chances.

Pickens agrees to disagree with Newsome. It's no surprise given the two had an on-field run-in with Newsome in a 2024 game when he was with the Steelers and Newsome with the Browns.

"Yeah, that's definitely how he should feel," Pickens said. via Patrik Walker of the team website. "Now, how we should feel, I'd definitely probably say a completely different story. But that's cool that he definitely thinks that. That's cool."

"I feel like he should definitely feel like that, but I feel like we're definitely not thinking the same thing."

Pickens does believe he and Lamb form the best wide receiver combo in the league, better than Brown and Williams, Cincinnati's Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins and the Rams' Puka Nacua and Davante Adams.

"Yeah, we definitely think we're the best," Pickens said. "Now, for everybody's brains and mindsets, I don't know what they're going to say. For us, yeah, we're the best."
